body.p: This chapter looks at two basic issues associated with indexes. First, we look at the pros and cons of having more than one index associated with a specific text. Then we explore the various types of indexes, which come in more flavors than just a typical name/subject index.

section.title: Numbers of Indexes
section.p: Indexessingle vs. multiple Multiple indexes Most books have a single, comprehensive index. But depending on the needs of the project, there may be two, three, or even more indexes associated with a particular text. Common arrangements include separating name indexes from subject indexes or using separate indexes for specialized content types such as legal cases or scientific names.

Multiple indexesproblems with The problem with multiple indexes is that users may not know which index to consult for a particular query. Multiple indexes also increase the chance that some items will be missed or duplicated.

section.title: Types of Indexes
section.p: Indexestypes of Name indexes Subject indexes Indexes come in many varieties. Name indexes list the names of persons, organizations, or other named entities mentioned in the text. Subject indexes organize concepts by topic. These are the two most common types, but many others exist.

Chemical indexes Alphabetizationof chemical indexes Scientific name indexes Chemical indexes present special challenges because chemical names do not always alphabetize in a straightforward manner. Scientific name indexes similarly require knowledge of naming conventions and taxonomic hierarchies.

Citation indexes Science Citation IndexScience Citation Index First-line indexes Alphabetizationof first-line indexes Geographic indexes Author indexes Legal case indexes Other specialized types include citation indexes (such as the Science Citation Index), first-line indexes used for poetry, geographic indexes, author indexes, and legal case indexes. Each type has its own conventions for organization and presentation.
Biographies, qualifiers in indexes of In indexes of biographical works, qualifiers are often needed to distinguish between individuals with the same name.
